paper.title: Algorithm 917: Complex Double-Precision Evaluation of the Wright omega Function
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 38(3), Apr 2012, Article 20 (per the frame item and the shipped 917.head). The ACM article was not fetched.
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/917.zip (article not fetched; ACM page not used)

code.commit: netlib CALGO archive 917.zip (C/Src: wright.c, wright.h, Makefile; C/Drivers: driver.c, test_boundary.c, Makefile, results.dat)
code.archive: downloaded by scout 2026-11-27 from netlib.org/toms/917.zip (zip, 35896 bytes, 9 entries). Extracted into a scratch directory under /tmp/scout_probe_917 (not committed); no code run by scout.
code.archive_sha256: not computed by scout; the reference is quoted from the shipped C/Drivers/results.dat
code.note: Build C/Src/wright.c with C/Drivers/test_boundary.c (Makefile: cc -I../Src, link -lm). test_boundary writes Results.dat in its working directory; the claim is one row of that file. Record the compiler and flags. The Makefile's diff_boundary target diffs the regenerated file against results.dat; that full diff is informational, not the claim.

claim.location: C/Drivers/results.dat inside 917.zip, first row: '-2.000000 6.283185 -3.689001 3.962752' (columns: Re z, Im z, Re omega(z), Im omega(z)). test_boundary.c generates this row at z = nextafter(-2.0,1.0) + i*nextafter(2*pi,-1.0), region 1 boundary, i=0.

reference.sha256: not computed for the member; the values are quoted here and compared as numbers

claim.paper_value: The ACM article was not read; the claim is the code's own shipped reference output, not a value located in the paper.
claim.metric: Re and Im of wrightomega_ext's w (the function value) at the test_boundary.c first point, compared componentwise with -3.689001 and 3.962752 from results.dat (printed with %f, six decimals).
claim.determinism: deterministic (fixed inputs in test_boundary.c; no random numbers)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. results.dat prints six decimals, so print rounding is 5e-7. Compiler and libm differences in the last ulps of a well-conditioned evaluation are far below 1e-5. A wrong branch, region or algorithm changes the value by far more. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 2 minutes: compile two C files and run test_boundary (3200 evaluations, under a second).
cost.data_size: none (inputs are hard-coded; results.dat is 122553 bytes and is not needed as input)
cost.data_licence: Netlib CALGO archive; use under the ACM/TOMS redistribution terms of the archive. The rerun should record it.

why: The code evaluates the complex Wright omega function by region-specific approximations and the shipped boundary driver prints the values; the number depends on the implemented approximation and is not a closed form checkable on paper.
